# DRAFT: VA Form 21-4138, Section II Remarks

> **Private draft.** It is in `personal-records/`, which is gitignored. Prepared 2026-10-08, only from what Marcus said in conversation that day.
> **Before signing:**
> 1. Read every sentence. Delete or change anything that isn't exactly true, or isn't how you would say it.
> 2. Fill in every [bracketed] item from your own memory and records. If you don't know something, write "I don't remember" or delete the sentence. Don't guess.
> 3. Have James York review it.
> 4. Copy the text into the Section II "Remarks" field of the official form (va.gov/find-forms/about-form-21-4138). Section I takes your identifying information.
>
> This statement is signed under penalty of perjury. Only what's true goes in.

---

RE: Supplemental Claim SC4806891. Correction and clarification of the August 2026 hospital records.

I submit this statement to correct the record about two emergency room visits in August 2026. I recently submitted the records from these visits. What I told the hospital staff at the time was not accurate, and I want VA to have the truth.

1. WHAT CAUSED THE OVERDOSES. Both overdoses, on August 4, 2026 and August 5, 2026, were caused by 7-hydroxymitragynine ("7-OH"), a concentrated kratom extract that acts as a potent opioid. The August 4 records describe an accidental overdose of gabapentin. That is not accurate. 7-OH was the cause. [Optional, only if true: describe what you told staff about gabapentin and why.]

2. MY 7-OH USE. I had been using 7-OH heavily for about two years before these overdoses, at very high doses. I spent more than $30,000 on it, and at the time I was spending about $500 per day. I still struggle with using it. [State your current use or treatment status here, accurately.]

3. WHAT HAPPENED DURING THE OVERDOSES. I took toxic doses. I began convulsing and losing control of myself. I became agitated and hostile, and I was angry and abusive toward my wife. [Add or correct details only from your own memory.]

4. MY STATE OF MIND. At the time of these overdoses I was having suicidal thoughts. I felt hopeless and did not care whether I died. [If you know whether you intended to die, say so. If you don't know, say that.]

5. WHY THE HOSPITAL RECORDS ARE DIFFERENT. At the hospital I minimized how much I had used and denied having suicidal thoughts. I did this because [state your real reason or reasons in your own words]. The records reflect what I told staff then, not what was actually happening.

6. NOW. I am not at current risk of suicide, but I have suicidal thoughts every day. [Optional: what you're doing for treatment and safety, if you want to include it.]

I am providing this so that VA has an accurate and complete record. The hospital records from August 4 and August 5, 2026 should be read together with this statement.

---

**Signature and date:** on the official form only (Items 9 and 10).
